absent: Locking discipline, concurrency rules and interrupt safety for all interfaces.
Implementation of IDE ioctl handling, error returns and privilege checks.
HPET driver behaviour, timing accuracy and interrupt routing.
Hardware breakpoint allocation, ownership and interaction with debuggers.
I2C adapter behaviour, transfer execution, retries and error reporting.
ICMPv6 checksum computation, packet validation and socket interaction.
Drive identity retrieval path and security state transitions beyond opcode values.

findings.text: Six device security operations occupy consecutive codes. SECURITY_SET_PASSWORD takes hex BA, SECURITY_UNLOCK takes hex BB, SECURITY_ERASE_PREPARE takes hex BC, SECURITY_ERASE_UNIT takes hex BD, SECURITY_FREEZE_LOCK takes hex BE, and SECURITY_DISABLE_PASSWORD takes hex BF.
Geometry record contains heads followed by sectors each sized as one byte, then cylinders sized as two bytes, then start sized as a native long word.

Early IDE controls assign HDIO_GETGEO to hex 301, HDIO_GET_UNMASKINTR to hex 302, HDIO_GET_MULTCOUNT to hex 304, HDIO_GET_QDMA to hex 305, and HDIO_SET_XFER to hex 306. Hex 303 has no assignment in these fragments.

Middle IDE queries assign HDIO_OBSOLETE_IDENTITY to hex 307, HDIO_GET_KEEPSETTINGS to hex 308, HDIO_GET_32BIT to hex 309, HDIO_GET_NOWERR to hex 30A, HDIO_GET_DMA to hex 30B, HDIO_GET_NICE to hex 30C, HDIO_GET_IDENTITY to hex 30D, HDIO_GET_WCACHE to hex 30E, HDIO_GET_ACOUSTIC to hex 30F, and HDIO_GET_ADDRESS to hex 310.

Bus and drive controls assign HDIO_GET_BUSSTATE to hex 31A, HDIO_TRISTATE_HWIF to hex 31B, HDIO_DRIVE_RESET to hex 31C, HDIO_DRIVE_TASKFILE to hex 31D, HDIO_DRIVE_TASK to hex 31E, and HDIO_DRIVE_CMD to hex 31F.
HDIO_DRIVE_CMD_AEB is defined as an alias that evaluates to the same number as HDIO_DRIVE_TASK, so both names select identical behaviour.

IDE modifier controls assign HDIO_SET_MULTCOUNT to hex 321, HDIO_SET_UNMASKINTR to hex 322, HDIO_SET_KEEPSETTINGS to hex 323, HDIO_SET_32BIT to hex 324, HDIO_SET_NOWERR to hex 325, HDIO_SET_DMA to hex 326, and HDIO_SET_PIO_MODE to hex 327.

Remaining IDE modifiers assign HDIO_SCAN_HWIF to hex 328, HDIO_SET_NICE to hex 329, HDIO_UNREGISTER_HWIF to hex 32A, HDIO_SET_WCACHE to hex 32B, HDIO_SET_ACOUSTIC to hex 32C, HDIO_SET_BUSSTATE to hex 32D, HDIO_SET_QDMA to hex 32E, and HDIO_SET_ADDRESS to hex 32F.
Bus power signalling defines three ordered levels with BUSSTATE_OFF as zero, BUSSTATE_ON next, and BUSSTATE_TRISTATE last, implying values zero through two.
Interface bus can rest disabled, energized, or floated. Transitions are requested through bus state set, bus state query and tristate operations, with reset providing recovery to a known condition.
Presence of __NEW_HD_DRIVE_ID marks that the expanded drive identity record described alongside is the active definition for consumers of this header.

Drive identity record is a large ordered collection of two byte words plus embedded text and arrays. It opens with configuration and retired geometry, vendor bytes, serial text of twenty, buffer and ECC words, firmware text of eight and model text of forty, multisector and capability bytes, validity words, current geometry, multisector state, total sector counts, DMA and PIO timing words, reserved ranges, queue depth, revision numbers, feature support and enable words, ultra DMA word, erase timing, power and acoustic words, streaming parameters, a wide 48 bit capacity, further reserved ranges, lock state, feature options, CFA and media serial areas, and closes with an integrity word.

Identity record fixes serial storage at twenty characters, firmware revision at eight characters and model at forty characters. Reserved spans cover word pairs and larger blocks, and the final word packs a checksum alongside a signature, so total length is fixed by the header.
Scheduling hints assign IDE_NICE_DSC_OVERLAP to zero, IDE_NICE_ATAPI_OVERLAP to one, IDE_NICE_0 to two, IDE_NICE_1 to three, and IDE_NICE_2 to four.

Timer block descriptor holds requested interrupt frequency, a flags word, a block selector and a timer selector. Frequency and flags each use native long width, selectors each use two byte width, in that sequence.

Timer interface marks periodic capability with HPET_INFO_PERIODIC as hex 10 and caps block count with MAX_HPET_TBS as eight. Control requests use the h family with numbers one through six for interrupt enable, interrupt disable, information query returning the descriptor, periodic enable, periodic disable and frequency programming accepting a long interval.

Timer interrupt delivery toggles between enabled and disabled, while periodic mode toggles independently between enabled and disabled. Frequency selection configures the rate used when interrupts fire.

Hardware watch lengths run from one through eight bytes, with HW_BREAKPOINT_LEN_1 taking one, HW_BREAKPOINT_LEN_2 taking two, HW_BREAKPOINT_LEN_3 taking three, HW_BREAKPOINT_LEN_4 taking four, HW_BREAKPOINT_LEN_5 taking five, HW_BREAKPOINT_LEN_6 taking six, HW_BREAKPOINT_LEN_7 taking seven and HW_BREAKPOINT_LEN_8 taking eight.

Access kinds assign HW_BREAKPOINT_EMPTY to zero, HW_BREAKPOINT_R to one, HW_BREAKPOINT_W to two, HW_BREAKPOINT_X to four, HW_BREAKPOINT_RW to three as read combined with write, and HW_BREAKPOINT_INVALID to seven as combined access plus execute.
Transfer descriptor orders a two byte device address, a two byte control flags word, a two byte payload length, and a pointer to payload bytes, in that sequence.

Transfer flags assign I2C_M_RD to hex 1, I2C_M_TEN to hex 10, I2C_M_DMA_SAFE to hex 200, I2C_M_RECV_LEN to hex 400, I2C_M_NO_RD_ACK to hex 800, I2C_M_IGNORE_NAK to hex 1000, I2C_M_REV_DIR_ADDR to hex 2000, I2C_M_NOSTART to hex 4000, and I2C_M_STOP to hex 8000.
Capability bits assign I2C_FUNC_I2C to hex 1, I2C_FUNC_10BIT_ADDR to hex 2, I2C_FUNC_PROTOCOL_MANGLING to hex 4, I2C_FUNC_SMBUS_PEC to hex 8, I2C_FUNC_NOSTART to hex 10, and I2C_FUNC_SLAVE to hex 20.

Higher capabilities assign I2C_FUNC_SMBUS_BLOCK_PROC_CALL to hex 8000, I2C_FUNC_SMBUS_QUICK to hex 10000, I2C_FUNC_SMBUS_READ_BYTE to hex 20000, I2C_FUNC_SMBUS_WRITE_BYTE to hex 40000, I2C_FUNC_SMBUS_READ_BYTE_DATA to hex 80000, I2C_FUNC_SMBUS_WRITE_BYTE_DATA to hex 100000, I2C_FUNC_SMBUS_READ_WORD_DATA to hex 200000, I2C_FUNC_SMBUS_WRITE_WORD_DATA to hex 400000, I2C_FUNC_SMBUS_PROC_CALL to hex 800000, I2C_FUNC_SMBUS_READ_BLOCK_DATA to hex 1000000, I2C_FUNC_SMBUS_WRITE_BLOCK_DATA to hex 2000000, I2C_FUNC_SMBUS_READ_I2C_BLOCK to hex 4000000, I2C_FUNC_SMBUS_WRITE_I2C_BLOCK to hex 8000000 and I2C_FUNC_SMBUS_HOST_NOTIFY to hex 10000000.

I2C_FUNC_SMBUS_BYTE unions read byte with write byte, I2C_FUNC_SMBUS_BYTE_DATA unions its read and write halves, I2C_FUNC_SMBUS_WORD_DATA unions its halves, I2C_FUNC_SMBUS_BLOCK_DATA unions block read with block write, I2C_FUNC_SMBUS_I2C_BLOCK unions I2C block read with write, I2C_FUNC_SMBUS_EMUL unions quick plus byte plus byte data plus word data plus process call plus block write plus I2C block plus packet checking, and I2C_FUNC_SMBUS_EMUL_ALL extends that with block read and block process call.

Small data carrier is a union holding either one byte, one two byte word, or a block array sized to the standard maximum of thirty two plus two extra slots where the first slot records length and the spare preserves user compatibility.

Direction assigns I2C_SMBUS_WRITE to zero and I2C_SMBUS_READ to one. Transaction selectors assign I2C_SMBUS_QUICK to zero, I2C_SMBUS_BYTE to one, I2C_SMBUS_BYTE_DATA to two, I2C_SMBUS_WORD_DATA to three, I2C_SMBUS_PROC_CALL to four, I2C_SMBUS_BLOCK_DATA to five, I2C_SMBUS_I2C_BLOCK_BROKEN to six, I2C_SMBUS_BLOCK_PROC_CALL to seven and I2C_SMBUS_I2C_BLOCK_DATA to eight.

Version six control header starts with one byte type, one byte code and a two byte checksum, followed by a four byte variant area. The variant can be viewed as one 32 bit word, two 16 bit words, four bytes, an echo pair of identifier plus sequence, a neighbour advertisement flag set, or a router advertisement triple.

Convenience aliases map identifier and sequence onto the echo pair, pointer plus MTU plus unused onto the 32 bit word, maximum delay onto the first 16 bit word, datagram length onto the first byte, router plus solicited plus override plus reserved onto advertisement flags, and hop limit plus managed plus other plus lifetime plus preference onto router advertisement members. Advertisement and router flag layouts swap bit order between little and big endian builds.

Control types assign ICMPV6_DEST_UNREACH to one, ICMPV6_PKT_TOOBIG to two, ICMPV6_TIME_EXCEED to three and ICMPV6_PARAMPROB to four, with ICMPV6_ERRMSG_MAX at 127 and ICMPV6_INFOMSG_MASK at hex 80. Informational types assign ICMPV6_ECHO_REQUEST to 128, ICMPV6_ECHO_REPLY to 129, ICMPV6_MGM_QUERY to 130, ICMPV6_MGM_REPORT to 131, ICMPV6_MGM_REDUCTION to 132, ICMPV6_NI_QUERY to 139, ICMPV6_NI_REPLY to 140, ICMPV6_MLD2_REPORT to 143, ICMPV6_DHAAD_REQUEST to 144, ICMPV6_DHAAD_REPLY to 145, ICMPV6_MOBILE_PREFIX_SOL to 146, ICMPV6_MOBILE_PREFIX_ADV to 147, ICMPV6_MRDISC_ADV to 151, ICMPV6_MRDISC_SOL to 152 and ICMPV6_MSG_MAX to 255.

ICMPV6_ROUTER_PREF_MEDIUM takes zero, ICMPV6_ROUTER_PREF_HIGH takes one, ICMPV6_ROUTER_PREF_INVALID takes two, ICMPV6_ROUTER_PREF_LOW takes three, ICMPV6_NOROUTE takes zero, ICMPV6_ADM_PROHIBITED takes one, ICMPV6_NOT_NEIGHBOUR takes two, ICMPV6_ADDR_UNREACH takes three, ICMPV6_PORT_UNREACH takes four, ICMPV6_POLICY_FAIL takes five and ICMPV6_REJECT_ROUTE takes six.
Four headers declare single inclusion guards that record their user API identity and prevent repeated processing when included multiple times.

Retired identity query returns a truncated length and must not be used for full discovery. Direct memory safe transfer marking is restricted to kernel space, and several transfer and capability flags are valid only when the adapter advertises the matching mangling, ten bit, no start or block capabilities.

User control enters through numbered IDE modification and query operations plus timer block controls for interrupts, periodic mode and frequency. Message transfer enters through the address flags length plus buffer descriptor, with small data union and transaction selectors shaping System Management Bus exchanges, and network control enters through the version six header types.

Headers publish stable user visible contracts for disk geometry and identity, timer block management, hardware watch configuration, bus transfer descriptors with capability masks, and version six control messaging.
